# the_librarian

> A skill librarian MCP server. Agents never load a skill collection into
> context: they describe a task in plain language, the librarian recommends the
> few skills that fit (local semantic search with diversity and anti-repetition),
> and agents report outcomes back so the collection curates itself from usage.
> Fully local: Ollama embeddings, SQLite storage, optional Apple on-device
> reranking. Python, single file, MIT.

Key facts:
- Problem solved: every installed skill costs context tokens on every request
  and overlapping descriptions cause wrong triggering; the librarian replaces
  always-loaded skills with one on-demand tool call.
- Tools: librarian_find (ranked shortlist for an intent), librarian_brainstorm
  (diverse sweep + wildcards), librarian_report (agent files worked/failed),
  librarian_reindex (rescan changed SKILL.md files), librarian_stats (curation
  digest: hot skills, never-surfaced, low success rate).
- Agents have no write access beyond the append-only outcome log; curation
  decisions stay with the human.
- Works with any MCP client over stdio (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor,
  Goose, and others). Requires Python 3.12+, the mcp SDK 2.x, and Ollama with
  nomic-embed-text.
- In production since 2026-06-10; usage numbers are published in the repo.
